target_customer: People with criminal records seeking jobs (70 Million Jobs) and later a community and AI agent service (Commissary Club); employers and advertisers paid
problem: Roughly 70 million Americans have a record and struggle to find work; the original product was a job board for them.
business_model: Employer-paid job board and staffing (70 Million Jobs); advertising, sponsorships and premium services (Commissary Club)
product_category: Fair-chance job board, later community and AI assistant

founders.name: Richard Bronson
prior_employers: Stratton Oakmont (left to found a brokerage)
previous_startups: Brokerage founded after leaving Stratton Oakmont (ended in a securities fraud conviction)
founders.background_notes: YC page: Wall Street background and prison time for securities violations; Wikipedia gives the Stratton Oakmont link.

exit.reason: Bronson attributed the closure of 70 Million Jobs to COVID hiring freezes and the Great Resignation, saying the company lacked resources to weather it.

technical_complexity.rationale: A job board with SMS alerts for applicants who lack laptops; ordinary web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A niche employer network of fair-chance hirers helped, but generic job boards could add the same filter.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows a large job board copying the niche; the company closed in 2022 citing the pandemic.

market_need_then: The YC launch post (2017-08) cites 70 million Americans with criminal records and notes applicants often lack laptops or easy internet access.

branding.name_origin: Named for the roughly 70 million people in the United States with a criminal record (Wikipedia).

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven, community supportive per the Commissary Club site.

branding.brand_signature: The number 70 million in the name

rebrands.why: New social network for people with records, widening market and services; the jobs business was kept as one arm.

branding.community_and_virality: Fast Company, KingsCrowd and Republic coverage; 676 investors backed the 2020 Republic campaign; Commissary Club says it was picked for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Startup Battlefield.

brand_strength.rationale: The name states the mission and drew press and crowdfunding support, though no merch or viral evidence was found.

pivots.from: Job board for people with records
pivots.to: Commissary Club social network, later an AI agent community
pivots.why: Wider needs of formerly incarcerated people; pandemic hit the job board

outcome_analysis: 70 Million Jobs raised about 1.4 to 1.7 million dollars from named investors plus a 2020 crowdfunding round, then closed in June 2022. Founder Bronson blamed pandemic hiring freezes and the Great Resignation, which cut revenue while resources were too thin to wait it out. The Commissary Club brand was launched in 2020 as a wider network and is being revived as an AI community in 2025 and 2026.
notes: Funding rests on Republic page text seen in a search result (the page itself returned 403) and the single investor list is undated with no amount; total raised was reported as over 1.4M and later 1.7M. YC marks the company Inactive while the revived Commissary Club site is live; the exit records the 2022 closure of 70 Million Jobs. Competitor list left empty: Honest Jobs appears in search but no source dated near the 2017 batch was found. Education of founder not found.
